question: Should Gateway support scheme-level extension origin wildcards such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if yes should they live in `allowedOrigins` or a separate constrained pattern surface?
rationale: This changes the browser-origin authorization boundary for Control UI/WebChat connections and the safe grammar is a product/security choice, not a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve a constrained pattern contract
options.body: Specify the allowed schemes and wildcard positions first, then implement the chosen contract across runtime matching, schema/help/docs, security audit, and regression tests.

options.title: Exact origins only
options.body: Keep current policy limited to explicit extension IDs and route users to exact-origin fixes such as the existing extension/custom-scheme PRs.

options.title: Defer to loopback-pattern work
options.body: Let the loopback `allowedOriginPatterns` PR settle first, then decide whether extension schemes need a separate follow-up grammar.

recommendation.title: Approve a constrained pattern contract
recommendation.body: Specify the allowed schemes and wildcard positions first, then implement the chosen contract across runtime matching, schema/help/docs, security audit, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest feature-history signal on Gateway browser-origin hardening and explicit non-loopback origin policy.
